title: Red Red
subtitle: Ghanaian black-eyed pea stew with fried plantain
excerpt: Red red is one of Ghana's best-known dishes -- a spiced black-eyed pea stew cooked in palm oil and tomatoes, served with slices of fried ripe plantain. The two reds in the name refer to the palm oil and the tomatoes. It is simple, filling, and deeply satisfying.
sourceNotes: Red red is a staple dish in Ghana. It is sold by street food vendors, cooked at home, and served in chop bars (informal Ghanaian restaurants) across the country. The dish is cheap, nourishing, and historically important as a source of protein for people across all economic backgrounds.

recipe.freezeNotes: The bean stew freezes well. Fry the plantain fresh.
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the stew easily.

content.text: Use ripe plantains -- the skin should be yellow with black spots. Unripe green plantains are too starchy and will not caramelise properly when fried. If plantain is not available, sweet potato works as a substitute.

items.prepNote: deseeded and blended with the tomatoes
use red palm oil if available
use 2 ripe plantains, peeled and sliced on the diagonal

content.text: Blend the tinned tomatoes and red pepper together until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large pot. Cook the onion for 7 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and ginger. Cook 2 minutes.
Pour in the blended tomato and pepper. Add the chilli flakes and salt. Cook for 12 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce thickens and darkens.
Add the black-eyed peas. Stir to coat. Simmer for 8 minutes until heated through and the sauce clings to the peas.
Fry the plantain slices in a separate pan with a little oil for 2 minutes per side until golden and caramelised.
Serve the bean stew with the fried plantain alongside.

items.cause: Tomato base not cooked down enough
items.fix: Cook the tomato sauce for longer -- it should be very thick before the beans are added

items.cause: Plantains are not ripe enough or oil is not hot enough
items.fix: Use very ripe plantains with black-spotted skins and make sure the oil is hot before adding
Stir gently and only heat the beans through -- they do not need to cook, just absorb the sauce

content.text: Red red is Ghana's national comfort food. It is sold in every chop bar and by street vendors in cities and rural areas alike. It is cheap, nutritious, and deeply popular. The fried plantain is not optional -- it is part of the dish. The combination of the savoury spiced beans with the sweet caramelised plantain is the whole point.
